review_evidence: README presents the repository as a Lean-centered cross-domain formal proof artifact and documents a large Mathlib-based formal corpus.
564 of 569 Lean files contain theorem/lemma/example/axiom declarations, with 5,224 declaration hits in the hydrated snapshot.

Representative FSOT/Theorems.lean declarations cover scaling, observer/quantum scalar behavior, and positivity/bounds; regardless of surrounding scientific interpretation, these are unique formal statements/proofs and cannot be losslessly filtered by repository role.
summary: Reviewed FSOT-2.1-Lean; retain its extensive Lean theorem corpus.

summary: Surveyed all 493 listed files (sizes, sha256, declaration counts via grep, generator headers) and read in full 13 files spanning 8 generators plus the root module, and read the opening sections and declaration lists of the largest core files. All 493 files hold distinct Lean declarations except FSOT.lean, which re-exports Formal-layer names with an export command. The ~478 generated *Priors.lean files follow per-generator templates with shallow proofs (decide/norm_num numeric facts about domain constants), but each file declares uniquely named defs and theorems with its own values and links to the core raw_S sign lemmas from FSOT.Formal.Domains. No file is byte-identical to another and none is import-only or empty, so FILTER-004 gives no content-level ground for hard exclusion. Shallow generated content is at most a downranking candidate under FILTER-002/FILTER-021. Default disposition: retain all.
